SYM and Alt shortcuts that open apps and commands
Hold SYM or Alt and press a letter to open what is assigned to it. Both use the same assignment list.
Smart toggle: Alt off after an opening
With Alt locked, typing an opening quote or bracket with Alt (\" ( [ {) switches Alt off, so the words inside come out as letters
Smart toggle: Ctrl off after a shortcut
A tapped Ctrl switches off after one shortcut such as copy, paste or undo; cursor and selection moves keep it on
Show dev-build updates, calibration, debugging and preview tools. On in dev builds
Trackpad debug and the release notes preview
Dev-build updates and tools for calibrating, debugging and previewing the keyboard. Most people never need them.
Termux and other terminals: Alt and SYM type symbols, Ctrl stays Ctrl

A terminal tells keyboards it has no text field, so Alt and SYM would go to the terminal and Pastiera\'s symbols wouldn\'t work. In terminal mode Pastiera types into it like a text field without suggestions, corrections or automatic capitals: Alt and SYM type Pastiera\'s symbols, and Ctrl, held, tapped or latched, reaches the terminal as a real Ctrl (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D…). Enter, Backspace, Tab, Esc and the arrows go to the terminal as they are.
In the apps below: Alt and SYM type Pastiera\'s symbols, Ctrl stays Ctrl
Learn nothing from anything you type: no new words, predictions, emails or numbers, and no recent emoji or symbols
Learn nothing in fields that ask keyboards not to, such as private browser tabs
For a minute after you copy text, a new text field offers it as a suggestion; typing dismisses it. Text marked sensitive (a password manager\'s) is only offered in password fields
A password field offers what you just copied, including from a password manager, as ⎘ •••••••• (never the text itself). It\'s kept in memory only, never in the clipboard history
An emoji for the word you\'re typing, e.g. 🍕 for pizza. Picking it adds the emoji after the word.

Make your own Device SYM layer: what each key types with SYM, and with Alt when Alt uses the Device SYM layer. A profile can replace a keyboard\'s own layer automatically, and Pastiera\'s backup includes it.
Tap a key to set what it types. Leave it empty to type nothing.

Each LED has its own colour: dim when off, the colour when active, brighter and more saturated when locked.

Active: held, or the emoji layer · Locked: tapped for one symbol, or the symbols
Active: held · Locked: tapped for one symbol, or the symbols
Active: held · Locked: tapped for one emoji, or the emoji layer or picker
Back to the suggested blue, orange, green and purple.
Emoji for chatting, work, social media, food, travel and more; or your own
A profile puts 26 emoji on the emoji layer, one per letter key, for a situation. Apply one to make it your emoji layer; edit single keys in Customize SYM layers.

The emoji layer follows the app you\'re in: Chatting in messengers, Social media in social apps, Work in work apps, Food and drink in food apps, Travel in maps and travel apps. Other apps keep your own layer.
Save the emoji layer as a profile
Keep the emoji layer as it is now, to switch back to later.
From a profile shared from Pastiera.

No keyboard bar in any app. The keys work as usual (Alt layer, SYM, Ctrl shortcuts, corrections), and the emoji and symbols pages still open on their keys.
The status LEDs still show where they usually are, drawn over the app, so you can see Shift, Alt, Ctrl and SYM.

Swipe across the keys to move the terminal\'s cursor a character at a time; swipe up or down for the commands before and after (the arrow keys). Nav Mode (double-tap Ctrl) works in terminals too: its keys move the cursor there.
With the keyboard hidden, its status LEDs still show where they usually are, so you can see Shift, Alt, Ctrl and SYM.
Like the Linux desktop: Pastiera stays out of sight in terminals. Alt still types your Alt layer and SYM its symbols, unseen; Ctrl stays Ctrl. The clipboard and emoji picker show while open.
A locked modifier\'s LED sweeps a gradient between its colour and a more intense version, so a lock is hard to miss.
What your emoji key does in terminals

Show or hide the extra keys row

Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt and arrows in the bar\'s place, from the menu, a shortcut or the emoji key in terminals. While the row is open, Q to P press its keys, left to right. Terminals and other apps each have their own set.
Pick up to %1$d keys, in the order you want them. The letter beside each is the key that presses it.
The terminal\'s Alt (hold with another key)

Edit this symbol layer. Hold to edit variations.
Apps where what you type stays as typed: SSH, code, AI agents

In these apps nothing rewrites what you type: no auto-correct, text replacements, auto-capitals, double-space full stop or automatic spaces. Suggestions still show, and only change a word when you pick one.
Also where apps ask for no suggestions
Fields that tell keyboards not to suggest (code editors, terminals, some search boxes) get exact typing too
Choose an app where every character should stay as typed
The row that opens with ☰. Switch buttons on or off; the higher a button is in this list, the further left it sits. The close button always comes first.
Move up (further left in the bar)
Move down (further right in the bar)
Suggestion bar words in bold, easier to spot at a glance
Links you copy lose their tracking (utm_, fbclid, YouTube\'s si…) right on the clipboard, so they\'re clean wherever you paste them, and open the full site rather than the mobile one
Ctrl+Shift+Q, W or E: the left, middle or right suggestion
Ctrl+1, 2 or 3: the left, middle or right suggestion (number row)
Recent emoji first on the layer
The emoji you used last take the layer\'s first keys, and its own emoji move along. Emoji you type from the layer count too.
A pick you undo straight away makes swipes need a little more; a swipe that falls short before a pick makes them need a little less.
Suggestion swipes back to your setting
After %1$d s without typing, a swipe scrolls instead of picking
Turn Scroll assistant on: the phone only passes keyboard swipes to Pastiera while it\'s on. Leave Swipe mode on scrolling: custom swipe actions take the swipes for themselves.
